info.long_name: Total number of students enrolled
info.short_description: Total students enrolled in the grade assessed, the denominator for the accompanying rates.
info.long_description: Total enrollment in the assessed grade as published by CDPH ('Total Number Students' in the kindergarten table, 'Total Students' in the 7th-grade tables). It is the denominator every rate in the same file is taken over. Not always a measured count: where CDPH printed an upper bound instead ('<35' in the 2019-20 7th-grade table) this column holds that bound, and where CDPH withheld the figure altogether it is empty. Read flag_enrolled before treating a value here as a count.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} students were enrolled in the assessed grade.

info.long_name: Whether N_enrolled is a count, a bound, or withheld
info.short_description: Empty where CDPH published an enrollment count; 'bottom_coded' where N_enrolled holds an upper bound CDPH printed instead ('<35'); 'suppressed' where CDPH withheld it and N_enrolled is empty.
info.long_description: CDPH de-identifies small jurisdictions two ways, and they are not equally informative. A BOUNDED cell states a limit -- '<35' students, '<=5.0%', '>=95.0%' -- which is a fact about the county, so the value column carries the bound CDPH printed and this flag reads 'bottom_coded' or 'top_coded'. Such a value is a limit, not a measurement: 'bottom_coded' means the true figure is at or below it and 'top_coded' that it is at or above it, so averaging or ranking it as though it were measured overstates the one and understates the other. A WITHHELD cell states nothing -- 'N/A', '--', '---', printed where the jurisdiction has under 20 enrollees (35 for 7th grade) -- so the value is empty and this flag reads 'suppressed'. The flag is empty where CDPH published an ordinary measurement. For N_enrolled specifically, the only bounded form CDPH uses is '<35' in the 2019-20 7th-grade table, so this flag takes 'bottom_coded' but never 'top_coded': a small enrollment is bounded from above, never from below.
info.statement: In {location}, the enrollment count is {value}.

Not the same denominator question as rate_conditional/rate_pme/rate_other_lacking/rate_overdue: those categorise WHY a student is not up to date, while this is coverage FOR ONE antigen specifically, and the two need not sum to 1 against each other. Not carried for 7th grade, where the comparable figures are rate_conditional_tdap etc. in standard/data_grade7.csv.gz.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} of students were up to date for 4+ dose DTaP vaccination.

flag_varicella.short_description: Empty where CDPH published a measured 2+ dose varicella coverage rate; 'top_coded' where `rate_varicella` holds the bound CDPH printed instead (CDPH bounds this measure from ABOVE only, since it is a coverage rate typically near 100 percent, so 'bottom_coded' is supported but does not occur here); 'suppressed' where CDPH withheld it and `rate_varicella` is empty.
flag_varicella.long_description: CDPH de-identifies small jurisdictions two ways, and they are not equally informative. A BOUNDED cell states a limit -- '<35' students, '<=5.0%', '>=95.0%' -- which is a fact about the county, so the value column carries the bound CDPH printed and this flag reads 'bottom_coded' or 'top_coded'. Such a value is a limit, not a measurement: 'bottom_coded' means the true figure is at or below it and 'top_coded' that it is at or above it, so averaging or ranking it as though it were measured overstates the one and understates the other. A WITHHELD cell states nothing -- 'N/A', '--', '---', printed where the jurisdiction has under 20 enrollees -- so the value is empty and this flag reads 'suppressed'. The flag is empty where CDPH published an ordinary measurement.
flag_varicella.statement: In {location}, the 2+ dose varicella coverage rate is {value}.

ca_school_immunization.name: California Kindergarten and 7th Grade Immunization Assessment
ca_school_immunization.location: CDPH annual assessment Report Tables (XLS): kindergarten admission status 2019-20 through 2024-25 and first grade 2022-23 (Table 2); kindergarten per-vaccine coverage for the same years and grades (Tables 3-4, position varies by year); 7th grade admission status 2018-19 through 2021-22 and 8th grade 2021-22 (Tables 3 and 4)
ca_school_immunization.description: County-level immunization status of California school entrants, taken from the county tables CDPH publishes with each year's immunization assessment report. standard/data.csv.gz stacks BOTH cohorts CDPH assesses -- kindergarten (and first grade, 2022-23) and 7th grade (and 8th grade, 2021-22) -- on the shared (geography, time, grade) key, matching the convention used for Connecticut: it is the file scripts/build_all_states_county_standard.R and scripts/generate_measure_info.R both read by that exact name, so it has to carry every measure column rather than either cohort alone. A kindergarten row therefore has no value in the 7th-grade-only columns (rate_conditional_tdap etc.) and a 7th-grade row has none in the kindergarten-only ones (rate_conditional, rate_dtap etc.) -- structurally, not from missing data. Two narrower files sit beside it with those structurally-empty columns dropped: standard/data_kindergarten.csv.gz (kindergarten 2019-20 through 2024-25, first grade 2022-23) and standard/data_grade7.csv.gz (7th grade 2018-19 through 2021-22, 8th grade 2021-22). Every figure is CDPH's own county aggregate rather than a roll-up of school-level data, so each series is produced one way. The kindergarten cohort combines TWO of CDPH's county tables for the same students: an admission-status table (rate_conditional, rate_pme, rate_other_lacking, rate_overdue) and a separate per-antigen coverage table (rate_dtap, rate_polio, rate_mmr, rate_hep_b, rate_varicella), joined on county/year/grade and cross-checked to report the same enrollment. For 2019-20 through 2022-23 the two tables come from different CDPH workbooks; where a duplicate row for the same county/year appeared in the vaccine table at two different levels of rounding (a paste error in CDPH's own spreadsheet, isolated to Yuba county 2019-20), the full-precision copy was kept and the rounded copy dropped. The 7th-grade assessment publishes one table per vaccine over the same students, so the Tdap and varicella measures are carried on a single row with a _tdap / _varicella suffix over one shared enrollment; CDPH published no 7th-grade varicella county table for 2018-19, so that year's varicella columns are empty and their flags are empty too, no cell having been censored. CDPH stopped publishing 7th-grade report tables after the 2020-22 round, so 2021-22 is the last 7th-grade year available. Each admission-status table also carries a 'Students with All Required Immunizations' / 'Entrants with Vaccine' overall coverage column; that combined figure is not carried here, only the per-antigen kindergarten breakdown. The CHHS Open Data school-level files reach back to 2013-14 but are deliberately not used to extend either cohort: their percent column is integer-rounded and their count column is suppressed on most rows, so a county rate rebuilt from them differs from the published one by a median of 0.5 to 0.8 percentage points, against quantities that are themselves usually under 3 percent.
ca_school_immunization.restrictions: Public data (California Department of Public Health). Small jurisdictions are de-identified by CDPH: figures for fewer than 20 enrollees (35 for 7th grade) are withheld outright, and values are bounded at 95, 98 or 99 percent for jurisdictions with 20-49, 50-99 and 100-499 enrollees respectively. Every measure carries a flag_<measure> column recording which case applies. Where CDPH printed a bound, the value column holds that bound and the flag reads 'bottom_coded' or 'top_coded' -- such a value is a limit, not a measurement, and averaging or ranking it as though it were measured will bias the result. Where CDPH withheld the figure the value is empty and the flag reads 'suppressed'; nothing is imputed for it. An empty value must not be read as a zero, and a flagged value must not be read as a measurement.
